facts.claim: "Somewhere for Something (Second Wind Version)" is track 6 of the 7-track album Second Wind by Pawns or Kings and runs 4:31.
Second Wind was released to streaming services on November 18, 2022. The Bandcamp page lists a December 16, 2022 release date.
The streaming release carries the credit line ℗ 2022 Pawns or Kings / U-NXT and was distributed through Ingrooves.
Pawns or Kings posted on Lemon8 that they wrote 'Somewhere for Something' for a girl who dumped them afterward, and that the song later went viral.
An earlier acoustic performance of the song, called a brand new song at the time, was filmed as Backyard Sessions Part 3. Ed and Ben played it in the Missouri woods.
The group is fronted by Ed Stengel, with Ben Bigelow as his music partner and producer. Both play a range of folk instruments on the recordings.
Pawns or Kings is based in Strafford, Missouri. Their Bandcamp bio says the music embodies the feeling of the Ozark Mountains and uses driving banjo with 3-part harmonies.
The band began as an indie folk act and later moved into dark, gritty country. Its stated goal was to bring world respect to the music traditions of the Ozarks.
The band's early bio says its members were formerly in Race to Olvido. Ed Stengel is the lead vocalist and lead songwriter, and Ben Bigelow handles recording, mixing and mastering.
Earlier releases include the debut album Letters to Lucy and Pomme de Terre (December 2013). Later releases include An Ozark Gothic (2024), a compilation.

draft:
A fingerpicked acoustic line opens **Somewhere for Something (Second Wind)**, patterned and a little country, while a second guitar strums chords underneath. A walking bass arrives, then a shuffle with a snare set forward in the mix. Each new part steps in rather than swells, and the room around them stays dry. Nothing is pushed or squashed. It sounds like people playing near one another.

Pawns or Kings have said plainly where the song came from. They wrote it for a girl, she dumped them afterward, and the song went viral. That sequence holds the feeling. A love song is an offering, written while the hope is still live, and this one outlasted the hope it was made for. Strangers picked it up and kept it. Pride and hurt sit side by side in that, and neither cancels the other: something made for one person ended up mattering to many, just not to the one it was meant for. The title carries a little of that ache too, a reaching toward a place and a purpose that stay unnamed.

Ed Stengel, the band's lead singer and songwriter, keeps his voice clear and mid-range, with a slightly raw edge that the production leaves alone. There's no gloss smoothing the seams. That rawness matters here. A cleaner take might sound like a man past the breakup. This one sounds like he's still standing in it.

The song has lived more than one life. An earlier version, introduced at the time as a brand new song, was filmed as Backyard Sessions Part 3, with Stengel and his partner and producer Ben Bigelow playing it out in the Missouri woods. On the album *Second Wind* it comes back with a rhythm section, and the name fits. It's the same confession, given more legs.

The band works out of Strafford, Missouri, and has spent years trying to win respect for Ozark music traditions. Their Bandcamp bio talks about capturing the feeling of the Ozark Mountains. They started in the indie folk revival and later moved into darker, grittier country, the turf they now call gothic country. This track sits near the warmer end of that path. The walking bass and the shuffle lean toward old country dance-hall bones, while the fingerpicking and the plain room sound keep it front-porch folk. Bigelow handles the recording, mixing and mastering, and his restraint is a choice. He lets the wood and the strings carry the weight.

Underneath the easy groove is a song that was handed to someone and set back down, and you can hear it still looking for the place it was meant to land.
